### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eb610038494e1b3ecf10ae2a58b3a8a58453fa37` — the merge of head `e55180423b73ccd293b94bbf3a99a204373089ca` into base `c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eb610038494e1b3ecf10ae2a58b3a8a58453fa37 && git checkout eb610038494e1b3ecf10ae2a58b3a8a58453fa37
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f e55180423b73ccd293b94bbf3a99a204373089ca && git checkout -B drift-repro c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f && git merge --no-ff e55180423b73ccd293b94bbf3a99a204373089ca

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `da8d0047c452a6041e9ba83f9d10f4db38397993`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Read: the diff `origin/main...refs/review/pr-23687` (4 files), the files at head, card #23661 with triage 6191456192, claim 6192818834, dev report 6194916763 and regrade 6194960134, the PR body, and the head's check-runs. Line numbers are at head. Nothing was built, tested or re-run locally.

1. **Authoring-path coverage, and the "synchronous before the save returns" claim. NON-BLOCKING: the claim holds.**
   - Every door that changes the runtime object the registry serves emits `onMetadataMutation` after its registry write:
     - `saveMetaItem`: write-through at `protocol.ts:23239-23247`, emit at `:23272`, then it returns.
     - Per-item publish and `publishPackageDrafts`: both go through `runPublishSideEffects` (callers `:24302`, `:25956`), which writes through at `:24737` and emits at `:24827`.
     - `rollbackMetaItem`: write-through at `:28805`, emit at `:28855`.
     - `revertCommit`: restore at `:28337` and `:28454`, then emit `deleted` at `:28364` or `active` at `:28487`.
     - `deleteMetaItem`, which covers reset-to-baseline and draft discard: heal at `:29636`, emit at `:29669`; the legacy exit emits at `:29872`.
     - `deletePackage` (uninstall) calls `deleteMetaItem` per row (`:26500`). `importUnmanagedPackage` goes through `saveMetaItem`.
     - A cluster peer replays through `applyRemoteMetadataMutation`: it converges the registry first (`:7752`, `:7760`), then calls `notifyMutationListenersLocal` (`:7766`).
     - Draft saves emit state `draft`. The listener correctly skips them (`plugin.ts:514`), because a draft never enters the registry.
   - Paths that do not emit the event. None of them leaves a live runtime object's exposure stale:
     - `reassignOrphanedMetadata` (adopt-orphans) rebinds an object row's `package_id` but does not re-register the object (`protocol.ts:27686` has `if (type !== 'view') continue;`). The registry and the copy keep the old binding together until restart. The copy never diverges from what is served, and `enable` is not touched.
     - `installPackage` and late manifests register code packages, which `bridgeManifestObjectsToMetadataService` handles.
     - The service's own `subscribe('object')` path runs from the service into the registry, so there the copy is the source.
     - A disabled package is refused by the engine (`registry.ts:5359` `isObjectPackageDisabled`), not by the copy.
   - **The synchronous claim is true wherever the service has `registerInMemory`.** The call chain:
     - `notifyMutationListenersLocal` calls each listener synchronously (`protocol.ts:7541-7552`).
     - `followRuntimeObjectCopy` (`plugin.ts:2380-2399`) starts the async `settleRuntimeObjectCopy`, which runs synchronously up to its first `await` (`:2414`).
     - That `await` is on `mirrorRuntimeObject` (`:2437-2443`), whose body runs synchronously into `putObjectCopy` (`:2459-2465`).
     - `putObjectCopy` calls `registerInMemory`, a synchronous Map set (`metadata-manager.ts:887-896`).
     - So the refreshed copy is in place inside `emitMetadataMutation`, before `saveMetaItem`, publish or rollback returns.
   - The claim does not hold for a service without `registerInMemory`: the `register` fallback (`:2464`) is async and persists through writable loaders. No in-tree occupant of the slot lacks the method. `IMetadataService` declares it optional (`spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.ts:295`), and `MetadataManager` implements it.
   - The delete limb is async: it runs after `await getObject` (`:2417`). The PR states this, and the engine refuses the deleted object's data verbs during that window.
   - The pin does not by itself prove "before the save returns". `copyOf` (test `:199-202`) awaits `listObjects` before `getObject`, so a refresh that landed a few microtasks late would also pass. The claim is proven by reading the code, not by the pin. NON-BLOCKING.

2. **Safety of the delete limb. NON-BLOCKING at this head; a residual for the maintainer, see ③.**
   - **Default composition** (`MetadataPlugin`'s `NodeMetadataManager` with no datasource loader). This path is race-safe:
     - `unregister`'s storage loop (`metadata-manager.ts:1458-1478`) touches no loader, and step 2 drops the in-memory entry synchronously.
     - The three guards are evaluated synchronously against the state at the moment of the call: state is `deleted` (`plugin.ts:2427`); the registry no longer serves the name (mirror returns false at `:2414` and `served` is undefined at `:2419`); the existing copy is tenant-authored (`:2418`).
     - A re-creation that lands during the awaits after the delete is mirrored back in (`:2429`).
     - Code-package copies are excluded: they carry `_provenance: 'package'`, and the tests pin them by identity (test `:255-273`, `:301-322`).
   - **With a writable `datasource:` loader.** A `DatabaseLoader` is attached only by an explicit `setDataEngine` / `setDatabaseDriver` opt-in (`metadata-manager.ts:632-678`), and nothing in-tree calls either. `DatabaseLoader.delete` removes the first `sys_metadata` row that matches `{type, name}`, with no state, package or scope filter (`database-loader.ts:718-724`, `:1538-1553`). On such a kernel there are two concrete paths:
     - (a) Deleting the active row of an object that still has a pending draft. `deleteMetaItem` removes only the row at `targetState` (`protocol.ts:29444`, `:29501`), and the limb then removes the surviving draft row.
     - (b) A re-creation whose row is written between the guards and the loader's `findOne` loses its stored row. The re-mirror at `:2429` restores only the in-memory copy, not the row.
   - Neither path is reachable in any in-tree boot.
   - On such a kernel the boot bridge (`plugin.ts:2308`) already persists every bridged registry object, code objects included, through that loader (`metadata-manager.ts:829-845`), so this setup is already broken before this PR.
   - The precedent `plugin-security/src/security-catalog-echo.ts:118-124` accepts the same bound.
   - Another tenant's row: `sys_metadata` carries no organization scope (ADR-0131 D6/D7, and `baseFilter` ignores it), and `deleteMetaItem` refuses an organization-scoped delete first (`protocol.ts:29270`). So no cross-tenant path exists beyond the loader residual above.

3. **Fail-open window and log level. NON-BLOCKING.**
   - `enforceApiExposure` falls open when a definition is absent or unreadable (`mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts:263-265`, `:280-305`). This PR leaves that unchanged, and leaves open question A open, which is correct for this card: no consumer-side change.
   - A live runtime object can still have an absent or stale copy after this PR in four cases:
     - (i) A service without `registerInMemory`: an async window plus persistence. None exists in-tree.
     - (ii) The `.catch` path (`:2385-2398`). For a live tenant-authored object the mirror path throws only if the registry read or a Map set throws. `isTenantAuthored` is a property read and cannot throw (`metadata-core/src/code-artifact-provenance.ts:43-45`).
     - (iii) `environmentId` kernels: unchanged, tracked as #23689.
     - (iv) A pre-existing mismatch. A legacy object-overlay row over a code-package object was hydrated at boot, but the service already held the package copy, so the bridge skipped it: the copy says the package body while the registry serves the overlay. New object overlays are refused on every topology (`protocol.ts:22220`, the package door), so (iv) cannot arise after boot, and this PR did not introduce it.
   - These windows are acceptable.
   - `error` is the right level under AGENTS.md "Degradation log levels". The registry and the service's copy disagree while the system looks normal, and what they disagree on is an exposure decision.
   - The message (`plugin.ts:2389-2397`) names the object, the consequence (readers keep the previous definition, and nothing retries) and the fix (restart; check that the service accepts in-memory registration).
   - It is logged once per failed event rather than once per process. Each failure concerns a different object or event, the same reason protocol.ts gives for not deduplicating its commit-store `error`. Acceptable.

4. **No consumer-side tolerance, no new public surface, `Clause-②: no`, and the code-package exclusion. NON-BLOCKING: all hold.**
   - The fix sits at the producer, in `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` only. `packages/mcp` and `metadata-protocol` are untouched, and no reader-side fallback is added. This meets the card's "no consumer-side tolerance".
   - The new members are private (`:2380`, `:2402`, `:2437`, `:2450`, `:2458`). The only added import is `isTenantAuthored` (`:5`), an existing export of `@objectstack/metadata-core`, which objectql already depends on. No export, schema or config field changes, and `packages/spec` is untouched.
   - The exclusion:
     - Mirroring requires the owner contributor to be tenant-authored (`:2439`). The protocol registers runtime rows with `_provenance: 'org'` (`protocol.ts:19437-19438`, `:30147-30148`), so a code-package owner never mirrors.
     - The `served` branch (`:2419-2425`) rewrites a copy held under a package object's name only when that copy is itself tenant-authored (the merged body of a removed legacy overlay). It replaces that copy with what the registry serves, which is the right direction.
     - It never touches a package copy the bridge wrote; the tests pin this at `:272` and `:318`.
     - `getObjectOwner` is keyed by FQN, but `computeFQN` returns the name unchanged (`registry.ts:172`), so short names resolve.

5. **The pins. BLOCKING: the type-check gate is red. Their substance is otherwise sound.**
   - **BLOCKING.**
     - What fails: the head's check-run `Type Check · workspace` (job 116488836291) is red. objectql's `typecheck` runs `check:test-typecheck`, which reports "src/plugin-runtime-object-metadata-copy.test.ts: 1 type error(s) in a file the ledger does not cover", and turbo ends with `Failed: @objectstack/objectql#typecheck`. `TypeScript Type Check` is red with it.
     - Why it is this PR: the merge-base `8d1fb1fb2d` is green on the same checks. Since then, main has changed only `protocol-commit-history.test.ts` and `spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` within objectql, core, metadata and spec sources, and this file's types depend on neither.
     - The cause, found by reading only: `const SYSTEM = ...` at `plugin-runtime-object-metadata-copy.test.ts:136` is never used in that file. `packages/objectql/tsconfig.test.json` inherits `noUnusedLocals: true` from the root `tsconfig.json:15`, so TS6133 fires.
     - This also contradicts the dev report's verification line, "objectql typecheck exit 0" (6194916763).
     - Consequence: the PR does not pass its own required type gate at this head.
     - Fix: delete line 136. Do not add the file to the debt ledger; expanding the ledger is maintainer-only.
   - **The objectql pins** assert:
     - toggled off after boot: the copy says `apiEnabled: false` and the listing agrees (`:229-241`);
     - created after boot: a copy exists (`:243-253`);
     - deleted: the copy and its listing entry are gone, and the package copy is the identical object (`:255-273`);
     - deleted then re-created during the delete-then-recreate race: the new copy survives (`:275-299`);
     - CONTROL: the package copy is untouched and the exposed neighbour still says it is exposed (`:301-322`).
   - Each precondition is asserted first (the boot copy is present at `:222-225`; in the dogfood pin, GATED is served before the toggle at `:332`), so no pin passes for an empty reason.
   - **The door pins** in `packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-stdio-runtime-object-exposure.test.ts` assert:
     - toggled off after boot: query, get, create, update and delete are refused with `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` / 404, the table is unchanged, and the neighbour is still served (`:329-349`);
     - created after boot with exposure off: refused from the first call (`:351-361`);
     - deleted: not listed and not described, data verbs answer `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, and the neighbour is still listed (`:363-377`);
     - CONTROL: an exposed object is fully served (`:312-327`).
   - **The ablations** match the test code:
     - Removing the call leaves the boot copies stale or absent, so pins 1 to 4 go red and CONTROL stays green: 4 failed, 1 passed.
     - Removing the re-mirror lets the released `unregister` drop the re-created copy, so only the race pin fails: 1 failed, 4 passed.
     - The door pins against the base dist: 3 failed, 1 passed, consistent with CONTROL not depending on the fix.
   - The card's "negative control that goes red when the fix is removed" is met by the one-time ablation, not by a permanent case. Both file headers declare this. Acceptable.

6. **Scope. NON-BLOCKING: holds.**
   - The diff touches four files: `.changeset/23661-runtime-object-metadata-copy.md`, `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/plugin-runtime-object-metadata-copy.test.ts` and `packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-stdio-runtime-object-exposure.test.ts`.
   - The dogfood file lies outside the claim's named paths; the report declares it under deviations. Dogfood declares `@objectstack/mcp`, `metadata`, `objectql` and `core` (`package.json:20`, `:21`, `:23`, `:48`).
   - Nothing touches `packages/mcp`, `protocol.ts` or `reassignOrphanedMetadata`.
   - The `plugin.ts` hunks sit at `:5`, `:515-518`, `:2280-2284` and `:2334-2465`. `start()` (from `:774`) and its region where the datasource mapping is installed before the first schema sync (held by #23649) are untouched.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql`: **patch**, which is correct.
- It is a bug fix that restores a declared contract: after boot, readers of `IMetadataService` now honour a runtime object's `enable.apiEnabled`.
- There is no export, signature, schema or config change, and every new member is private.
- The changeset declares `'@objectstack/objectql': patch` with `Clause-②: no` and no arm, which is consistent.
- The two test files publish nothing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Security boundary.** The fix closes a real exposure. The dev measured rows read and written through MCP stdio past `apiEnabled: false`, and `refuseUnexposedDataAction` answering ALLOWED. The fix brings both back to the declared contract. It narrows no declared acceptance set, because the refusals were already the specified behaviour.
- **`Clause-②: no`: confirmed.** No acceptance set is widened, no public surface is enlarged, and no (narrowing) arm applies.
- **Open question A** (whether both gates should stop falling open on an absent definition) is outside this PR. Recommendation A is coherent, given that this PR keeps a live runtime object's copy present and current. The decision belongs to the maintainer and is not made here.
- **Maintainer decision (a residual that does not block this head).**
  - The delete limb's `unregister` also deletes through writable `datasource:` loaders, whose delete is keyed only by type and name (`database-loader.ts:718-724`, `:1538-1553`).
  - No in-tree boot reaches this. On a control-plane kernel that opts in, it can remove a pending draft row or a just-re-created row.
  - `plugin-security/src/security-catalog-echo.ts` already accepts the same bound.
  - Whether `IMetadataService` should gain an in-memory-only removal is the maintainer's call. That would be new public surface: `Clause-②: yes`, minor.
  - Suggest a follow-up card rather than widening this PR.
- **Out of scope and correctly noted:** `environmentId` kernels (#23689), and copies of an uninstalled code package's objects (the dev's `out_of_scope_findings[1]`).
- **Verification honesty.** The report's "objectql typecheck exit 0" does not match the head's CI. For the fix head, the seat should require the green check-run rather than the report's word.

**Adoption note (seat).** The record comes from an isolated, read-only reviewer subagent at the contract-review tier, by the maintainer's 「契约复审 opus就够了」. The seat audited its transcript and adopts it. The reviewer used Bash for `git show` / `git diff` / `git log` / `git fetch` and unauthenticated GETs, two `get_job_logs` reads, and one local Write (this record). There was no build, test run, push or GitHub write, so `Local-runs: none` holds. The seat confirmed the blocking finding independently:
- `ci-failure.mjs --pr 23687` shows `TypeScript Type Check` and `Type Check · workspace` red at this head;
- `const SYSTEM` occurs once in the test file, at its definition (line 136).

The patch round is sent to the dev. The new head needs a fresh record.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e55180423b73ccd293b94bbf3a99a204373089ca`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

This is a delta review against the FAIL record at `da8d0047c452a6041e9ba83f9d10f4db38397993`.

- **The delta.** `git diff da8d0047c4 e55180423b` is one commit, `e55180423b` "test(objectql): drop an unused constant from the runtime-object copy pins". It deletes one line: `const SYSTEM = { context: { isSystem: true } } as any;` at `packages/objectql/src/plugin-runtime-object-metadata-copy.test.ts:136`. `SYSTEM` no longer appears anywhere in the file.
  - This is exactly the fix for the prior BLOCKING finding: the TS6133 unused local under the inherited `noUnusedLocals: true` (root `tsconfig.json:15`).
  - Nothing else moved. The PR surface is still the same four files.
  - `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` is byte-identical: blob `bff396ce5278a14a566c3fe3b0c581a8cd012867` at both heads.
- **CI at this head is still running.** `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1/6 to 6/6 and the Lint lanes are `in_progress`. `TypeScript Type Check` has not reported yet. This verdict judges the diff; the seat gates landing on CI separately.
- **Prior judgments 1 to 6 carry over unchanged**, NON-BLOCKING:
  1. Every authoring door emits `onMetadataMutation` after its registry write. Adopt-orphans does not re-register objects, but the registry and the copy stay consistent, so exposure is unaffected. The copy is refreshed synchronously before the save returns wherever the service has `registerInMemory`. The pin itself does not prove that timing.
  2. The delete limb is race-safe in the default composition. With a writable `datasource:` loader it can delete other rows of the same name; see ③.
  3. A live runtime object is left with an absent or stale copy only on a service without `registerInMemory` (none in-tree), on `environmentId` kernels (#23689), or in a pre-existing legacy-overlay case. The `error` log level and message are right.
  4. No consumer-side tolerance, no new public surface, and `Clause-②: no` is right. The code-package copy exclusion never wrongly touches a package copy.
  5. The pins assert the refusal after toggle-off, the deleted object not listed or described, and the CONTROL still working. Each precondition is asserted first, and the ablations are plausible. The type-gate blocker is fixed by this delta.
  6. Scope is the declared four files. The start-order region held by #23649 is untouched.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql`: **patch**, unchanged. It is a bug fix, with no export, schema or config change. The changeset still declares patch with `Clause-②: no`. The delta is test-only.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Clause-②: no`: confirmed.** Open question A (both exposure gates fall open on an absent definition) stays with the maintainer and is out of this PR.
- **Acceptance note for the maintainer: the delete-limb residual.**
  - `metadataService.unregister` also deletes through writable `datasource:` loaders.
  - `DatabaseLoader.delete` matches only on `{type, name}` (`database-loader.ts:718-724`, `:1538-1553`).
  - So on a kernel that opts in to a `DatabaseLoader` (`setDataEngine` / `setDatabaseDriver`), the limb can remove a pending draft row of a deleted object, or the stored row of an object re-created mid-race.
  - Nothing in the repo opts in, and `security-catalog-echo.ts` already accepts the same bound.
  - Adding an in-memory-only removal to `IMetadataService` would be new surface (`Clause-②: yes`). Suggested as a follow-up card.

**Adoption note (seat).** This is the same isolated, read-only reviewer at the contract-review tier, resumed for the delta. The seat audited the delta run: 5 tool uses, all reads (`git show` / `git diff` / `git rev-parse`, unauthenticated check-run GETs), plus the local Write of this record. There was no build, test run, push or GitHub write, so `Local-runs: none` holds. The seat confirmed the delta independently: `git diff da8d0047c4 e55180423b` is one deleted line in the test file, and `plugin.ts` is the same blob at both heads. The FAIL record 6195385587 at `da8d0047c4` is superseded for this head. CI at this head is gated separately, before the ACCEPT.
